**Description of problem:**
The new open window sensors for Tado thermostats do not switch to "true" if an open window was detected. Maybe this is because I still use a V2 Tado bridge?



**Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml` entries and (fill out even if it seems unimportant):**

comments: Hey there @michaelarnauts, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`tado`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L333) for? Thanks!

This was contributed by @gppanayotov in https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/pull/30090 Maybe he knows more?

I don't use the open window detection, so I can't test with mine. Is Bridge V2 the one where you need a subscription? It probably won't work on that bridge.

> This was contributed by @gppanayotov in #30090 Maybe he knows more?
> 
> I don't use the open window detection, so I can't test with mine. Is Bridge V2 the one where you need a subscription? It probably won't work on that bridge.

No it doesn't work with mine and I don't use the subscription but still have access to the auto away, window etc...

The bridge V2 is the old one without Homekit support and without "forced" subscription. 

The "early start" sensor for Tado devices that was recently implemented does not work for me either, so I assume this bug is indeed related to the V2 bridge...

I have have the v3+ bridge (the one that requires subscription), I don't have an older version of the bridge so couldn't test it when I created the sensor. 
From what I can see  **"openWindowDetected": true** is available in the api only before it's activated, if you don't have a subscription a notification is displayed in the app and you have to click a button to turn the heating off (activate open window mode). 

So as of now Open Window sensor reports that window an open window is detected but Tado hasn't turn the heating off. Maybe we can extend it to report "true" when it's detected or activated any thoughts ? 

Can someone share the api state of a zone when window is opened with older version of the bridge ? 

Here is an example of the zone state when window is detected and when it's activated.
Before activation: 
"overlayType": null,
  "overlay": null,
  "openWindow": null,
  "openWindowDetected": true,


After activation: 
  "overlayType": null,
  "overlay": null,
  "openWindow": {
    "detectedTime": "2020-01-20T09:17:45Z",
    "durationInSeconds": 900,
    "expiry": "2020-01-20T09:32:45Z",
    "remainingTimeInSeconds": 824
  },

OK, we have found the root cause... 

For Tado V2, the API never returns `openWindowDetected` (since the bridge automatically activates the open window mode, i. e. turns off the thermostat), but it does return the `openWindow` object when the open window mode is active. 

Since the HA sensor only checks for `openWindowDetected`, it never switches to true in case of a V2 bridge and probably also for V3.

So basically it was a misunderstanding from my side since I thought the sensor would indicate that the open window mode already is active - is it possible to add this information also to the Tado implementation? 

I see the use case for `openWindowDetected` (for V3+ users), but this not relevant for V2 or V3 users...

So does this mean i need to replace my V3 bridge for a V3+ to detect an open window in HA?
Cause my OpenWindowDetected also seems to be always false, and i don't seem to have a "OpenWindow' Object. Or at least, if I do I don't know how to find it.

Should be fixed by https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/32564

Added additional coverage in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/32632 to verify
@cicero200272 This one is going to need another round before it gets fixed.  There is a bit more coordination that needs to happen before we can solve it for good.  Sorry for the delay
Updated HA to 0.107 and the open window detection works like a charm now. Thanks a lot!

review_comments:
As mentioned in the other PR, we should not assert state directly on the library device. We should only assert core state, eg entity state from the state machine. If we patch the library and test services it's ok to assert that the patched library is called correctly during the service call. Testing like this makes sure the tests are robust and we're not introducing code that is the device library's responsibility.

We're only interested in testing that home assistant interfaces correctly with the device library. We're not interested in testing the device library or device api itself. Testing the library or api is the responsibility of the device library.
I'm going to move all this into PyTado
